findings.title: Islands read bald — ground vegetation far too sparse for the stylized-AAA bar
findings.what: Across nearly every island the walkable ground is bare sand/grass with only scattered palms plus a thin sprinkle of tiny plants. Sea of Thieves shores are densely carpeted with continuous ferns, bushes, grass clumps and flower beds; here the interiors read empty/unfinished. Quantified from the captured world.json: Castaway Reach (r=88, ~24,300 m2) has 95 TOTAL props (palms+boulders+barrels+foliage), so effective ground-cover foliage density is roughly 1 plant per 400-600 m2 — essentially bald between the few clusters.
findings.where: audit-noon3/05-rumrunner-key-shore.png (entire midground hillside is bare pale grass), 08-castaway-reach-shore.png, 03-the-crooked-atoll-shore.png, 10-booty-bay-shore.png, 07-mermaid-s-folly-shore.png; aerials 08-castaway-reach-aerial.png and 05-rumrunner-key-aerial.png show a thin dot-scatter over bald grass.
findings.root_cause_guess: src/server/world/MapGenerator.ts:1236 scatter target = min(110, max(12, radius*SCATTER_DENSITY*0.8)) is SHARED across palms/boulders/clutter AND foliage, so soft ground-cover is only a fraction of an already-capped budget. Only 1-3 tiny dense 'patches' are added (MapGenerator.ts:1186-1209: patchCount capped at 3, patchR 4.5-7.5m, <=14 plants each). The instanced grass (Game.ts:4045, min(2600, r*r*0.3) blades of 0.4x0.5) works out to ~1 tuft/10 m2 — far below turf coverage.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a dedicated soft-foliage ground-cover pass separate from the capped structural scatter (or raise SCATTER_DENSITY and lift the 110 cap for shape:'none' plants). Enlarge and multiply the dense patches (bump patchCount to scale with area, grow patchR, raise per-patch fill). Increase the grass InstancedMesh count 3-5x and lower alphaTest slightly so interiors carpet continuously.

findings.title: Grass tufts and wildflowers render as isolated green flecks / bare spikes, not turf
findings.what: The instanced grass reads as tiny isolated green 'X'/claw marks dotted on bare ground rather than clumped turf, and the wildflower prop renders as 3-5 bare vertical green stalks with almost no foliage — like green sticks poking out of the sand. Neither reads as vegetation up close.
findings.where: Zoom of 05-rumrunner-key-shore.png (ground around the barrel: isolated green splays on otherwise-bare grass) and 12-parley-point-shore.png (left ridge: a cluster of 4-5 tall bare green stalks that read as sticks).
findings.root_cause_guess: Game.ts:4046 grass blade is a single 0.4x0.5 cross-plane placed one-per-seed with no clumping (loop 4090-4109 scatters each blade independently and thinly, dRatio 0.06-0.84). build_plants.py build_wildflowers (lines 202-238) is thin cone stems with sparse tiny leaflets, so at scatter scale it silhouettes as bare green rods. Note the ferns already cluster (Game.ts:4137-4160) and read better — grass does not.
findings.suggested_fix: Cluster grass like the ferns: 3-6 blades per seed with small XZ jitter so each seed reads as a tuft; widen/lengthen the blade slightly and raise count. Give wildflowers denser leaf mass (more leaflets, a small basal clump) or fold them into the flower_patch bed prop rather than scattering singles.

findings.title: Small rocks/boulders render as near-black spikes that read as debris (not stylized stone)
findings.what: Small scattered rocks appear pure/near-black and pointy, clashing hard with the grey eroded boulders sitting right beside them and with the bright sand. On shorelines these read as black shards/'shark-fin' cones rather than sunlit stone — an obvious break from the stylized rock look the rest of the pass achieves.
findings.where: Zoom of 02-skull-cove-shore.png (two tall near-black rock spikes on the right by the water), 02-skull-cove-aerial.png and 11-gallows-sands-aerial.png (near-black cones intermixed with grey boulders), 01-smuggler-s-rest-shore.png (near-black cone with a foam ring at the waterline).
findings.root_cause_guess: boulder_c is authored with material 'Rock_Dark' (scripts/blender/build_rocks.py:153; _helpers.py:27 = linear 0.22,0.22,0.24) — markedly darker than the 'Rock_Grey' used by boulder_a/b, and it is the smallest, most-scattered boulder on rocky/volcanic/bone isles; flat-shaded with shadowed faces at that size it silhouettes near-black. The waterline black cones are the seaRock DARK FALLBACK (Game.ts:3521 darkMat 0x292d2b) which is hit when searock_c isn't ready at the one-time mesh build (Game.ts:3424-3428 builds+caches each rock exactly once, never rebuilding).
findings.suggested_fix: Retint boulder_c to 'Rock_Grey' (or ~0.30 linear) so small rocks read as stone. For the waterline cones, rebuild the seaRock mesh once its GLB has loaded (invalidate the seaRockMeshes cache entry when assets.clone returned null) or, at minimum, lighten the fallback darkMat so no pure-black cones appear.

findings.title: Bushes read as bright-green faceted gumdrops / top-down asterisks and never build into masses
findings.what: Individual shrubs (bush / flower_bush) appear as small bright-green faceted blobs dotted one-by-one on the sand; from above they read as flat green stars/specks. They pop as isolated lime gumdrops rather than aggregating into the layered bush masses SoT uses to green a shoreline.
findings.where: Zoom of 08-castaway-reach-shore.png (green gumdrop blobs across the hillside), 08-castaway-reach-aerial.png and 04-dead-man-shoals-aerial.png (bright-green blob dots / stars scattered thinly).
findings.root_cause_guess: build_plants.py leaf_clump (lines 30-48) is a few overlapping icospheres (radius*0.45-0.85) — a single small gumdrop — and the scatter places bushes as isolated singles (MapGenerator SCATTER_MIX) with no local clustering. The bush leaf albedos (Leaf_B 0.22,0.50,0.20 etc.) are bright/saturated so each blob pops against pale sand.
findings.suggested_fix: Place shrubs in 2-4 plant micro-clusters at generation time (mirror the fern clumping already in Game.ts:4137) with size variation so they merge into bush masses; slightly desaturate/darken the bush leaf materials so they read as foliage rather than lime candy, and let bushes overlap the palm bases to soften the isolated-object look.
